calls.title: Design System Cohort Kickoff
calls.summary: The team discussed implementing a design system through weekly jam sessions aimed at boosting collaboration between engineers and designers. They planned to hold these sessions on Fridays at 10 AM to avoid scheduling conflicts. The conversation included strategies for improving selector UI components, with engineers assigned ownership of specific types and an emphasis on reducing technical debt. Challenges with the multi-select component's complexity were highlighted, necessitating a refactor to clarify options. The team also committed to standardizing size naming for UI components, advocating for broader participation to ensure consistency and shared understanding across the product. Ongoing feedback was encouraged to adapt the approach over time.
calls.keywords: Design system, selector components, multi-select combo box, component sizing, UI consistency, design-engineering collaboration

calls.title: Design System Cohort Kickoff
calls.summary: A key focus of the meeting was to establish a strategy for implementing a design system, with dedicated weekly sessions for focused work on design components. Kari Kay proposed involving engineers in collaborative jam sessions to address backlog issues effectively. Initial efforts will focus on improving selector components, with specific variants assigned to individual engineers to manage complexity. Discussions highlighted the need to consolidate component logic and standardize sizing conventions for selectors and badges, favoring descriptive naming. The team recognized the complexity of the multi-select combo box due to color inconsistencies and proposed clear size definitions. Lastly, they agreed on the significance of broader participation and regular check-ins to avoid fragmented solutions and share knowledge across teams.
calls.keywords: Design system, selector components, multi-select, Radix UI, sizing conventions, component collaboration
